subject.title: feat(gateway): durable user profiles with email aliases and avatars

question: Should OpenClaw adopt durable user profiles, mutable email aliases, and stored avatars as a supported core shared-state and gateway-protocol contract for the identity program?
rationale: This PR introduces a new persistent identity model and public protocol/administration APIs; correcting the schema registration is mechanical, but accepting the long-lived product and compatibility contract requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve the bounded core profile contract
options.body: Keep profiles optional and additive, register their tables canonically, and merge after focused real behavior proof.

options.title: Keep durable profiles outside core
options.body: Decline this core persistence and protocol surface, leaving future shared-identity enrichment to a plugin or a narrower approved API design.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded core profile contract
recommendation.body: Keep profiles optional and additive, register their tables canonically, and merge after focused real behavior proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the canonical identity-program tracker and the adjacent merged identity implementations.
